question: Show that the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x)=3x-5$ is onto.
explanation:
Arbitrary element of the co-domain
Let $y\in\mathbb{R}$. To show that $f$ is onto, we seek $x\in\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x)=y$.

Determination of a pre-image
Solving
$$3x-5=y$$
gives
$$x=\frac{y+5}{3}.$$
Since $y\in\mathbb{R}$, we have $\frac{y+5}{3}\in\mathbb{R}$.

Verification
For $x=\frac{y+5}{3}$,
$$f\left(\frac{y+5}{3}\right)=3\left(\frac{y+5}{3}\right)-5=y.$$

Conclusion
Every $y\in\mathbb{R}$ has a pre-image in $\mathbb{R}$. Hence, $f$ is onto.

options.A: $f$ is not onto because negative real numbers have no pre-images
options.B: $f$ is onto because every $y\in\mathbb{R}$ has the pre-image $x=\frac{y+5}{3}$
options.C: $f$ is onto because every $y\in\mathbb{R}$ has the pre-image $x=\frac{y-5}{3}$
options.D: $f$ is not onto because $0$ has no real pre-image
